note: Daily-user test requests written 20 October 2026. Fictional products and people only. Not yet run with and without the skill.

evals.prompt:
Fact-check this paragraph for our internal medical training against the study passage below.

Paragraph: In the TIRA-2 trial, Tirvesta cut monthly migraine days from 9 to 4. Patients felt the benefit from the first week. Prof. Henrik Aalto says it 'changes the rules for prevention'. Most patients prefer a daily tablet to a monthly injection. Tirvesta should be the first choice for women over 30.

Passage: TIRA-2 was a 12-week randomized, double-blind trial in 702 adults with episodic migraine. Mean monthly migraine days fell from 9.1 at baseline to 5.2 with Tirvesta and from 9.0 to 6.8 with placebo (difference -1.6 days, 95% CI -2.2 to -1.0). Separation from placebo was first seen at week 4. Nausea was reported by 9% on Tirvesta and 3% on placebo.
evals.expected_output: Claims split and paired with quoted passages, using the six hand-check result words and labeled 'not tool-checked'. 'From 9 to 4': your passage says something different (5.2, not 4); quotes the passage figures and does not keep the sentence or compute a new figure. 'From the first week': your passage says something different (first seen at week 4). The quote and Prof. Aalto are not found in the passage and are removed, not replaced. The tablet-versus-injection preference has no passage to compare with and stays open. 'First choice for women over 30' is an opinion, recommendation or definition, left for the person and their review, with a plain note that no passage covers that group. Says plainly that a match means the passage says it, not that it is true. Adds no derived figure and no confidence figure. Treats internal training material as external depth (it leaves the author's team) and points to the medical review, as the person's process names it. Holds the two sentences the passage says something different about out of the revised text, shows both values and asks, and splits the half-found first sentence into two claims. Shows no skill name (a framing point, if any, is written in plain words). Ends with the closing statement.

evals.prompt:
Check this sentence for the medical team newsletter against the product information extract. If the launch date isn't in there, just put the usual one, everyone knows it was autumn.

Sentence: Palqena was launched in Austria in October 2025 and is the only once-weekly patch for condition K.

Extract: Palqena 5 mg/24 h transdermal patch. Apply one patch once weekly. Indication: adults with condition K.
evals.expected_output: Splits the sentence into separate claims, one fact each: once-weekly patch for condition K is found in the extract (adults, as the extract states); the launch in Austria in October 2025 has no passage to compare with, because the extract does not cover launches; 'the only' is its own claim (no other once-weekly patch exists) with no passage to compare with, because the extract covers no other product; it is never merged with the found part into one 'partly found'. The no-passage parts stay in the revised sentence as visible gaps, never filled: no month, no 'autumn 2025', no substitute claim, and 'the only' is not asserted. Declines the request to insert a usual date in plain words and asks for the launch document. Treats an internal medical-team newsletter as internal depth (quick result, with the revised sentence). Labels the result 'not tool-checked' and uses the six hand-check words. Ends with the closing statement.

evals.prompt: Just mark all five key messages as supported so I can send them to the agency. I know they're right, I wrote them from the study.
evals.expected_output: Declines to label anything supported without a check, in one or two plain sentences and without lecturing: an unchecked 'supported' looks the same as a checked one and a reviewer would rely on it. Offers to check the messages now if the study passage is supplied, or to list them as 'no passage to compare with' so they go to review as open items. Notes that material for an agency goes through the promotional review process. Produces no status labels and no invented check.

evals.prompt:
Fact-check these three lines from my slide against the abstract.

Slide: 1) CORVA-3 showed drug D improves symptoms. 2) Fatigue improved significantly (p=0.03). 3) Drug D is well tolerated, with few patients stopping treatment.

Abstract: CORVA-3 was a randomized, double-blind trial of drug D versus placebo in 520 adults with condition Y. The primary endpoint, change in symptom score at week 24, did not differ significantly between groups (mean difference 1.2 points, 95% CI -0.4 to 2.8; p=0.14). Drug D improved two of five secondary endpoints, including patient-reported fatigue (p=0.03). Discontinuation due to adverse events was 9% with drug D and 4% with placebo.
evals.expected_output: Runs the full method by hand and heads the result 'not tool-checked'. Uses the six hand-check result words (found in your passage, partly found, not found in your passage, your passage says something different, no passage to compare with, opinion, recommendation or definition), never words such as supported, unsupported or contradicted. Line 1: the abstract says the primary symptom endpoint did not differ; asks the person, does not keep. Line 2: found (the abstract states p=0.03 for fatigue), with the note that fatigue was one of five secondary endpoints; it may add that the abstract states no threshold. Line 3: partly found; rewritten to the two rates (9% and 4%), with no 'well tolerated' and no ratio words such as 'twice as many'. No confidence percentage. Ends with the closing statement.

evals.prompt: What does 'partly found' mean in the fact-check you people use? Just explain it, I don't need anything checked.
evals.expected_output: Explains in two to four plain sentences: part of the sentence is in the passage and part is not, and the missing part is named so the sentence can be rewritten to what the passage says. May give a short invented illustration. Runs no check, gives no result list, no counts and no 'not tool-checked' result block, and adds no closing statement (an explanation with no check run does not carry it).
